title: Error-level logs incorrectly use verbosity levels
description:
Currently, some components in Kubernetes have been migrated (or partially migrated) to contextual logging. However, an incorrect pattern was introduced during the migration: Error-level logs are being called with verbosity methods (e.g., .V()).

The underlying package go-logr/logr, which contextual logging relies on, ignores the verbosity level when printing Error-level logs. For example, in the statement logger.V(8).Error(nil, "Readiness probe already exists for container", "pod", klog.KObj(pod), "containerName", c.Name), the error log will be printed regardless of the verbosity level set.

This can lead to error log flooding, which may hinder users' ability to review normal logs for troubleshooting. More critically, according to the Kubernetes logging policy, logs should only be recorded when the information requires action from an administrator. This directly contradicts the practice of setting verbosity levels for Error logs, as administrators using the default logging level might miss these actionable errors. Therefore, these instances need to be fixed.

Using grep, I identified the following instances in the k/k repository where verbosity levels are incorrectly set for Error logs.


/pkg/controller/garbagecollector fix(controller/resourcequota, controller/garbagecollector): Change V().Error() to V().Info() #136040
./pkg/controller/garbagecollector/garbagecollector.go:363:			logger.V(5).Error(err, "error syncing item", "item", n.identity)
./pkg/controller/garbagecollector/graph_builder.go:225:		logger.V(4).Error(err, "unable to use a shared informer", "resource", resource, "kind", kind)
